related_questions.question: What is the fastest way to get rid of oral thrush?

text_blocks.snippet: The fastest way to get rid of oral thrush (candidiasis) is with antifungal medication prescribed by a doctor. This typically involves a topical treatment like a mouthwash (nystatin) or lozenges (clotrimazole). In more severe cases, oral medications like fluconazole or itraconazole may be necessary. While waiting for medication to take effect, maintaining good oral hygiene and addressing any underlying health conditions that may contribute to thrush are also important.
snippet_highlighted_words: antifungal medication prescribed by a doctor

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the fastest and most effective approaches:

list.title: Antifungal Medication:
list.snippet: Consult a doctor or dentist for a prescription. Topical treatments like nystatin mouthwash or clotrimazole lozenges are often the first line of defense. For more persistent cases, oral antifungals (fluconazole, itraconazole) may be prescribed.
Brush your teeth gently but thoroughly at least twice a day with a soft-bristled toothbrush.
Consider using a diluted hydrogen peroxide mouthwash (half water, half 3% hydrogen peroxide).
Clean or disinfect dentures daily.
Limit sugary and yeast-rich foods (candy, cookies, breads) as these can promote fungal growth.
Include probiotics like yogurt in your diet to help restore the balance of bacteria in your mouth.

list.title: Manage Underlying Conditions:
list.snippet: If you have diabetes, manage your blood sugar levels. If you have a compromised immune system, work with your doctor to address the underlying cause.
Saltwater rinse: Dissolving half a teaspoon of salt in a cup of warm water and swishing it around your mouth can help create an inhospitable environment for bacteria.
Apple cider vinegar: Diluted apple cider vinegar (one teaspoon in a cup of water) can be swished in the mouth to help combat the fungus.
Coconut oil pulling: Swishing a tablespoon of coconut oil in your mouth for 15-20 minutes can help reduce the fungal load.
Clove oil: Clove oil, either as a dietary supplement or mouth rinse, can be effective due to its antiseptic properties.
Consult a Doctor: It's crucial to see a doctor or dentist for diagnosis and treatment, especially if the thrush is severe or persistent.
Don't Delay Treatment: Oral thrush can spread to other parts of your body if left untreated.
Avoid Irritants: Avoid mouthwashes with alcohol or other harsh chemicals that can irritate the mouth.

text_blocks.snippet: Several medications can increase the risk of developing oral thrush, also known as oral candidiasis, a fungal infection in the mouth. Common culprits include antibiotics, corticosteroids (both inhaled and systemic), and chemotherapy drugs. Certain medications that cause dry mouth can also indirectly contribute to thrush, as saliva helps to keep the mouth clean and prevent fungal overgrowth, according to Everyday Health.
snippet_highlighted_words: antibiotics, corticosteroids (both inhaled and systemic), and chemotherapy drugs

list.title: Antibiotics:
list.snippet: Antibiotics disrupt the natural balance of bacteria in the body, including the mouth, which can allow the Candida fungus to overgrow and cause thrush.

list.title: Corticosteroids:
list.snippet: These medications, including inhaled forms used for asthma and COPD, and oral forms like prednisone, can suppress the immune system and create an environment where Candida can thrive.

list.title: Chemotherapy and other cancer medications:
list.snippet: Cancer treatments can weaken the immune system and cause mouth sores, both of which increase the risk of thrush, according to OncoLink.

list.title: Medications that cause dry mouth:
list.snippet: Antihistamines, antidepressants, certain medications for high blood pressure or heart failure, and some pain medications can reduce saliva production, making the mouth a more hospitable environment for Candida.

list.title: Inhaled corticosteroids:
list.snippet: Inhalers for asthma and COPD can lead to thrush if the medication residue is not cleared from the mouth after use.

list.title: TNF inhibitors:
list.snippet: These medications, used for autoimmune diseases, can also increase the risk of thrush.

list.title: Hormonal contraceptives:
list.snippet: While not directly causing thrush, hormonal birth control can alter the body's hormonal balance, which can indirectly contribute to yeast infections.

list.title: Other medications:
list.snippet: Medications like some anti-seizure drugs or certain cancer medications (like chemotherapy drugs or vinca alkaloids) can also be associated with an increased risk of oral thrush.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that many people carry the Candida fungus in their mouths without experiencing any problems. Thrush develops when something disrupts the natural balance, allowing the fungus to overgrow. If you are concerned about thrush or experience symptoms such as white, creamy lesions on the tongue or inner cheeks, consult with a healthcare professional for diagnosis and treatment.
